'''Shisho Shrine''' (四所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen|ja|城崎温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Onsen}}, {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en|Toyooka, Hyōgo|qid=Q696388|lt=Toyooka, Hyōgo}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}, adjacent to the public bath {{ill|Goshono-yu|ja|御所の湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshono-yu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135540751}} ("Gosho no Yu"), one of the town’s prominent hot springs.

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the principal deity {{ill|Yuyama-nushi no Kami|ja|湯山主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuyama-nushi no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (also rendered {{ill|Yuyama-no-Okami|ja|湯山主大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuyama-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, ゆやまぬしのかみ), accompanied by the {{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|ja|宗像三女神|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Sanjoshin|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses}}—{{ill|Tagorihime|ja|多紀理毘売命|2=ja|3=タキリビメ|4=fr|5=Takiribime|6=zh|7=多紀理毘賣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Takikuri-hime, 多岐里比売神), {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|多岐都比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タギツヒメ}} (Takitsuhime, 田記津比売神), and {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵島比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime||2=fr|3=Ichikishimahime|4=ja|5=イチキシマヒメ|6=zh|7=市寸島比賣命|8=ru|9=Итикишима-химэ|10=de|11=Ichikishima-hime}} (Ichikihime, 市杵比売神). Together they form the Four Shrine Gods (四所神). All are worshipped as protective deities of the hot springs and water, and the Three Munakata Goddesses are additionally venerated as water guardian deities.

== History ==
The shrine’s origins trace back to {{ill|Wadō (era)|en|Wadō (era)|qid=Q1373026|lt=Wadō era}} 1 ({{ill|708|en|708|qid=Q23511|lt=708}}), when a local official named Nisei Shimo Gongen (Nichisei Shitagenokami) founded the shrine in accordance with a divine revelation delivered in a dream by four deities. In {{ill|Yōrō|en|Yōrō|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yōrō era}} 1 ({{ill|717|en|717|qid=Q23532|lt=717}}), the monk {{ill|Dōchi|ja|道智|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōchi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} visited the shrine and received an oracle that led to the establishment of the {{ill|Mandarayu|ja|まんだら湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mandara-yu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135540745}} ("Mandara-yu"), the first hot spring bath in Kinosaki. Since then, the shrine has been revered as the guardian of {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen|ja|城崎温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Onsen}}, with the {{ill|Onsen-ji Temple|ja|温泉寺 (豊岡市)|lt=Onsen Temple|lt_ja=温泉寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11562944}} established by Dōchi serving as its head temple. During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu Hanzenrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1970535}} of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the shrine separated from its affiliated temple in the 3rd year ({{ill|1870|en|1870|qid=Q7741|lt=1870}}) and was officially reclassified as a village shrine in the 6th year (1873).

Behind the main hall, a renowned spring known as "Enmei-sui" (Life-Prolonging Water) flows continuously.

== Festivals ==
* '''{{ill|Kinosaki Onsen Festival|ja|城崎温泉祭り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Onsen Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' ({{ill|April 23|en|April 23|qid=Q2527|lt=April 23}}–{{ill|April 24|en|April 24|qid=Q2529|lt=April 24}}): Held in commemoration of the memorial day / anniversary of the enlightenment of the monk Dōchi Shōnin, the founder of Kinosaki Onsen.
* '''Kinosaki (Onsen) Dream Plaza''' ({{ill|July 23|en|July 23|qid=Q2722|lt=July 23}}–{{ill|August 25|en|August 25|qid=Q2819|lt=August 25}}, excluding Obon and weekends/holidays, from 20:00 to 21:00): Evening festivities, including small booths, super ball scooping, food stalls, and performance shows, are held in the shrine precincts. Additionally, during this period approximately 200 "Dream Fireworks" are launched for 5 minutes nightly beginning at 21:00 (except {{ill|August 10|en|August 10|qid=Q2779|lt=August 10}}–{{ill|August 16|en|August 16|qid=Q2812|lt=August 16}}).
* '''{{ill|Kinosaki Danjiri Festival|ja|城崎だんじり祭り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Danjiri Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' ({{ill|October 14|en|October 14|qid=Q2922|lt=October 14}}, Yoimiya – {{ill|October 15|en|October 15|qid=Q2919|lt=October 15}}, Main Shrine): A traditional festival with portable shrines and floats.

== Shrine Structures ==
The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 3 ({{ill|1928|en|1928|qid=Q19715|lt=1928}}) after the original buildings—along with ancient records—were completely destroyed and burned during the {{ill|1925 North Tajima earthquake|en|1925 North Tajima earthquake|qid=Q11401118|lt=1925 North Tajima Earthquake}} in {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō}} 14 ({{ill|1925|en|1925|qid=Q18107|lt=1925}}). The {{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=Honden}} is a {{ill|Sangensha Nagare-zukuri|ja|三間社流造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangensha Nagare-zukuri|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Sanmen-sha style), and the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=worship hall}} is an {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|qid=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri}} structure, both registered as cultural properties of Hyōgo Prefecture. In {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 56 ({{ill|1981|en|1981|qid=Q2437|lt=1981}}), renovations were carried out under the design and construction of {{ill|Wada Masaharu|ja|和田政春|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Masaharu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The original main hall, constructed in {{ill|Kan'en|en|Kan'en|qid=Q1145723|lt=Kan'en era}} 4 ({{ill|1751|en|1751|qid=Q7615|lt=1751}}), was made entirely of zelkova (keyaki) wood and was significantly larger.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Hyōgo Prefecture Designations ===
'''Registered Tangible Cultural Properties (Buildings):'''
* {{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=Main Hall}} (registered December 22, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 18 / {{ill|2006|en|2006|qid=Q2021|lt=2006}})
* {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=Worship Hall}} (registered December 22, 2006)

=== Toyooka City Designations ===
'''Cultural Properties:'''
* Benten-yama (Benten-zan) Hōkyōintō (Pagoda of Benzaiten Mountain), "Etchu Jirōbee's Grave" (one unit): A grave marker of {{ill|Echū Jirōbei|ja|越中次郎兵衛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Echū Jirōbei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, established in the {{ill|Northern and Southern Courts period (disambiguation)|en|Northern and Southern Courts period (disambiguation)|qid=Q8140349|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, {{ill|Ōan|en|Ōan|qid=Q1146245|lt=Ōan era}} 2 ({{ill|1369|en|1369|qid=Q6211|lt=1369}}); designated March 1, Shōwa 50.
'''Natural Monuments:'''
* Habitat / birthplace of {{ill|Euterpnosia chibensis|lt=Himeharuzemi|ja|ヒメハルゼミ|ceb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Euterpnosia chibensis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5976326}} (a cicada species; designated May 18, Heisei 2).

== Access ==
* 15-minute walk from {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen Station|en|Kinosaki Onsen Station|qid=Q1055689|lt=Kinosaki Onsen Station}} on the {{ill|San'in Main Line|en|San'in Main Line|qid=Q1135170|lt=Sanin Main Line}}.
